summary:
**Worked:** big human moments on Threads: the Lost Battalion rescue (1,698 views, 88 reactions), Outpost Snipe (15 comments, the most yet), and Greece says no (1,383). Living Cards keep winning: median 1,418 YouTube views, and YouTube views doubled week on week. Action first openings lifted TikTok hold from 32 to 43 percent (Test B).

**Didn't:** Story Cards (YouTube 22 to 259 views, Instagram hold 6 to 15 percent) and Home Front procedure like the draft lottery (Reach about 0.6). Threads also held back 8 posts in two weeks, including U-559 and Mount Rushmore.

**Tests:** A (human first Spec Sheet hooks) closed: Response doubled, Reach not clearly better. B closed with a TikTok gain. C (shorter, more intense Story Cards) starts with this Thursday's video run; review 24 Nov.

**Decisions:** Facebook versus Substack, Name This on Instagram, and whether to keep Tests A and B as standing practice. Your h-aid-britain veto is applied.

questions.ask: Facebook versus Substack in Buffer: what should happen to Facebook?
questions.why: Facebook cards drew a typical **2 views** over 30 posts. Facebook Reels drew a typical **277**, about as much as Instagram Reels, though 5 of 10 Living Card Reels drew almost nothing. Swapping Facebook for Substack would lose about 280 views a day. Claude's view: keep Facebook for Reels and stop the static cards there.
options: Keep Facebook for Reels only, stop the cards there
questions.if_yes: Claude updates the Roadmap and the run docs in the Project to match, and the runs follow from the next batch.
questions.if_blank: Facebook keeps getting every post, and the question comes back next week.

questions.why: The two week test is over. Four Name This cards drew 13, 5, 4, and 1 Instagram views, the same as Instagram cards (typical 5.5), and no follows. Claude's view: end it.
questions.if_yes: Name This posts go to X, Threads, and Facebook only, from the next Saturday Name This run.
questions.if_blank: Name This stays on Instagram and the question comes back next week.

questions.ask: Keep human first Spec Sheet hooks (Test A) and action first video openings (Test B) as standing practice?
questions.why: Test A: Response doubled (1.23 against 0.59), Reach not clearly better. Test B: TikTok hold rose from 32 to 43 percent, Instagram flat. Both cost nothing to keep. The runs keep doing both until you decide.
questions.if_yes: Claude updates the Cards and Videos docs in the Project so both read as the normal practice, not tests.
questions.if_blank: The runs keep doing both, and the question comes back next week.

questions.ask: Veto any of this week's new Code Room groups
questions.why: These 7 groups were added to the Code Room master list from posted cards. Veto any link you don't want dealt; vetoed groups are kept but never dealt and never added again. Leaving all of them alone is fine.

groups.link: Each honors service by Americans from a minority group.
Each involves a Medal of Honor earned in that very action.
Each involves a wartime secret the Allies guarded.
Each involves one of the largest machines of its kind ever built.
Each involves an ultimatum that was refused.
All three took place on or near Bougainville.

questions.why: Buffer gives no follower totals, so the first Tuesday of each month the review asks. Your 27 Oct counts: X 4, Instagram 11, Threads 21, TikTok 5, YouTube 8, Facebook 2.
A reply worth knowing about, something you saw in an app that Buffer can't, a subject you want more or less of. The research run reads this.
